candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate the response kinetics of CRP and ESR.

options.A: CRP generally rises and falls more rapidly than ESR as inflammatory activity changes.
options.B: CRP is specific for one diagnosis, whereas ESR is diagnostic of all inflammatory diseases.
options.C: ESR changes within minutes while CRP remains unchanged for weeks.
options.D: Neither test is affected by inflammation.

candidate.rationale: Both CRP and ESR are nonspecific inflammatory markers, but CRP changes more rapidly in response to inflammatory stimuli. CRP can rise within hours and decline promptly as the trigger resolves, whereas ESR typically rises more slowly and can remain elevated longer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CRP generally responds more rapidly than ESR to changes in inflammatory activity; both markers are nonspecific.
candidate.source_document_title: Acute Inflammatory Response; C-Reactive Protein: Clinical Relevance and Interpretation
candidate.source_locator: CRP rises within hours and changes rapidly; ESR rises over approximately 24–48 hours and decreases more gradually
candidate.stem: A nurse compares C-reactive protein (CRP) with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) for monitoring an inflammatory process. Which statement is accurate?
